title: A mine: cross-section of a machine for extracting water from the pit. Etching by Bénard after L.J. Goussier.
date: [between 1700 and 1799] (Wellcome); Minéralogie plate, Diderot/d'Alembert Encyclopédie style (my inference, not stated in the record)
depicts: Black-and-white engraved plate (Pl. IV). Top: a large undershot water wheel (water enters from the left at 'A', arrow) on a timber frame with six chain sprockets/pulleys; below ground level a deep timber-lined mine shaft in cross-section, hatched rock on both sides, with long vertical pump rods and chains running down the shaft and a stack of pump barrels on the right side (labels E, F, G, H). Scale bar 'Toises' at lower left. Bottom lettering: 'Minéralogie, Élévation de la Machine pour tirer les Eaux, aux Mines de Pontpéan.' Signed 'Goussier Del.' / 'Benard Fecit'. Shows exactly the problem Savery addressed: water having to be pumped out of a deep mine, here by water-wheel power.
